summary.text: Dale Strong is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A lifelong first responder in Monrovia, he served 26 years in Madison County government, first as a county commissioner and then as the commission's first Republican chairman. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Appropriations Committee, where he is Vice Chair of the Commerce, Justice, Science Subcommittee, and chairs a Homeland Security subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Strong was born in Monrovia, Alabama, the son of a founding member of the Monrovia Fire-Rescue Department. He graduated from Sparkman High School in 1988, according to Wikipedia, and earned a B.S. in business administration from Athens State University and an EMT license from the University of Alabama in Huntsville.

According to his official biography, he has spent his adult life as a first responder. He began as a junior volunteer firefighter and 911 dispatcher, and he has 35 years of service as an EMT and 41 years as a volunteer firefighter. Wikipedia adds earlier jobs in public relations at First Alabama Bank and as a sales representative for Solvay.

Strong served in local government for 26 years, starting as the youngest Republican elected official in Alabama and eventually becoming the Madison County Commission's first-ever Republican chairman, according to his official biography. Wikipedia says he was first elected to the commission in 1996 and became its chairman in 2012, serving until he resigned on January 2, 2023. The biography says he reduced the county workforce and improved department efficiency without raising taxes.

In 2022 he won the Republican nomination for the seat held by Rep. Mo Brooks, defeating Casey Wardynski in a June 21 runoff, 63.4% to 36.6%. He won the general election that November with 67.1% of the vote over Democrat Kathy Warner-Stanton and Libertarian P.J. Greer.

Strong was sworn in to the House in January 2023. He serves on the Appropriations Committee, with subcommittee roles as Vice Chair of Commerce, Justice, and Science, plus Transportation, Housing and Urban Development and Legislative Branch, and he chairs the Homeland Security Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee.
According to his official biography, he is married to Laura Toney Strong, and they have two children, Whitney and Harrison.
